title: Collective phases in overdamped magnetic self-propelled spherocylinders
abstract: We study the collective dynamics of self-propelled spherocylinders carrying magnetic dipole moments in two dimensions. Magnetic interactions are modeled as two opposite monopoles $\pm Q$ separated by a distance $\ell$ along the particle director, a dumbbell model that remains well-defined at short range and introduces an explicit geometric lever arm for the magnetic torque. This approach, combined with the elongated particle geometry, produces a torque that competes with steric alignment in a manner inaccessible to point-dipole or disk models. By independently varying monopole separation and dipole strength (parameters that map directly onto the geometry and magnetization of cylindrical magnets) we show that the system navigates a rich landscape of collective states: gas, polar flock, chain, vortex-alignment, and locked-dimer phases. Our results establish that particle elongation and distributed magnetic charge together provide a minimal, experimentally accessible set of tuning knobs for controlling coherent states in magnetic active matter, with direct implications for the design of self-organized magnetic microswimmers and active colloidal assemblies.
summary: This work investigates how magnetic interactions and particle shape dictate the collective organization of self-propelled microswimmers. By modeling the particles with a dumbbell charge structure, the authors map out five distinct phases—including flocking and vortex alignment—by tuning parameters related to magnetization and geometry.
main_problem: The study focuses on characterizing the collective dynamics and phase transitions of self-propelled spherocylinders carrying magnetic dipole moments in two dimensions.
main_result: The system exhibits a rich landscape of five distinct collective states—gas, polar flock, chain, vortex-alignment, and locked dimer—controlled by particle elongation and distributed magnetic charge.
method: The dynamics are modeled using overdamped equations of motion for position and orientation, solved via numerical simulations across parameter space.
model_or_system: The system consists of self-propelled spherocylinders interacting magnetically (modeled as $\pm Q$ monopoles separated by $\ell$) and sterically in 2D. The dynamics are governed by competition between propulsion, repulsion, and magnetic torques.
key_observables: Collective phases (gas, polar flock, chain, vortex-alignment, locked state), pair contact energies ($ ar{\epsilon}_{	ext{chain}}$, $ ar{\epsilon}_{	ext{blocked}}$), polarization ($P$), and vortex order parameters ($\Phi_V, \Phi_A$).
important_parameters: Three dimensionless groups control behavior: $\Pi_1$ (charge separation ratio), $\Pi_2$ (magnetic vs. propulsion angular velocity comparison), and $\Pi_3$ (steric force vs. self-propulsion).
main_assumptions: The dumbbell model is used to regularize the magnetic torque, avoiding divergences associated with point-dipole approximations at short range.
figures_summary: Figures map collective behavior across $(\Pi_1, \Pi_2)$ space, illustrating phase boundaries and showing how order parameters change between the five identified states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing equations of motion, introduces dimensionless control parameters ($\Pi_1, \Pi_2$), analyzes pair contact energies to define state transitions, and maps out the resulting phase diagram across varying parameter regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on classical active matter, the concept of controlling emergent collective states via tunable interaction potentials (magnetic/steric) is analogous to designing synthetic quantum Hamiltonians or engineered many-body systems in AMO physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Two interacting self-propelled spherocylinders (i, j) carrying magnetic dipole moments modeled as two opposite monopoles ±Q (positive in red, negative in blue) separated by a distance ℓalong the particle director.

FIG. 2: Steady-state configurations at Π3 = 150; particles are colored by orientation angle θ ∈(−π, π] using a cyclic HSV colormap (shared colorbar). A nearly uniform hue signals polar alignment, swirling opposing hues within a cluster signal vortex rotation, and random hues indicate disorder. Left: Representative snapshots of the four collective states. Chain (Π2 ≈0.8, Π1 ≈1.17): elongated quasi-linear aggregates driven by head-to-tail attraction, without vortex rotation or global polar alignment. Coherent vortex-alignment (Π2 ≈5.0, Π1 ≈1.17): intra-cluster vortex rotation. Polar flocking (Π2 ≈1.8, Π1 ≈0.67): global director alignment. Locked (Π2 ≈12.8, Π1 ≈0.83): dense compact aggregates...

FIG. 4: Phase diagram in the Π2 × Π1 plane for Π3 = 150. The four panels show the scalar order parameters: (a) polarization P; (b) vortex order parameter ΦV ; (c) vortex alignment ΦA; (d) weighted vortex alignment Φw A. White dots mark the 80 validated state points (Π2 ∈{0, 0.2, . . . , 16.2}, Π1 ∈{0, 0.17, . . . , 1.17}; state points with Π1 ≥1.33 are excluded; see the validity analysis in the Supplemental Material [42]). The black dashed line marks the contour |¯εchain| = 1 (see Fig. 3).

FIG. 3: Dimensionless two-particle contact energies ¯εchain (red), ¯εbend (blue), and ¯εblocked (green), normalized by F0Lr (Eqs. (7)–(8)), as a function of (a) Π1 and (b) Π2. In each panel, solid and dashed lines correspond to the limiting large and small values of the other parameter, respectively. Shaded regions in (a) indicate where each configuration is energetically accessible: chain only (pink), bent chain only (light blue), and dimer or blocked pair (light green). Insets in (b) illustrate the three contact geometries; red and blue circles denote positive and negative magnetic charges.

FIG. 5: Cluster size scale s∗in the Π2 × Π1 plane for Π3 = 150, with simulation snapshots superimposed at each of the 80 state points. s∗is the mean size of the largest cluster normalized by N = 500, ranging from disordered (light, s∗≈0) to fully aggregated (dark, s∗≈N). Labels indicate the observed collective regimes. The black dashed line marks the contour |¯εchain| = 1 (see Fig. 3); large-aggregate states (s∗≫1) lie predominantly above it, with gas and gas-and-cluster phases below.
